Each case must contain:
- case_id: string like "case_001"
- category: one of the letters A-J (defined below)
- category_name: descriptive name
- student_profile: object with name, education (list of strings), skills (list), experience (list), projects (list), certifications (list), summary (string)
- job: object with title, company, location, employment_type, description (full text), required_skills (list), preferred_skills (list), experience_requirement, education_requirements (list), responsibilities (list), posting_date (string or null), application_url, source_url
- ground_truth: object with expected_priority ("HIGH"|"MEDIUM"|"LOW"), expected_recommendation ("APPLY"|"APPLY_IF_TIME"|"LOW_PRIORITY"), expected_fit_range ([min, max] as 0-100), expected_risk_level ("LOW"|"MEDIUM"|"HIGH"), expected_opportunity_confidence_range ([min, max] as 0-100), key_signals (list of strings describing what system should detect)
- notes: string explaining why this ground truth is correct

Categories (aim for 2-3 cases each):
A. Legitimate + strong fit — well-known company, role matches student skills perfectly. Priority: HIGH
B. Legitimate + weak fit — real company, role doesn't match student well. Priority: LOW
C. Legitimate + medium fit — real company, partial skill overlap. Priority: MEDIUM
D. Old/questionable posting — posting date is months/years old. Priority: LOW
E. Cross-source inconsistency — conflicting details (salary, location, requirements differ). Priority: LOW or MEDIUM depending on fit
F. Strong student fit + opportunity concerns — great match but company/posting is questionable. Priority: MEDIUM (verify first)
G. Weak student fit + legitimate opportunity — great company, poor skill match. Priority: LOW
H. Missing official information — company exists but no career page found. Priority: MEDIUM
I. Conflicting information — description contradicts itself or differs from company info. Priority: LOW
J. Challenging/adversarial — 95% student fit, excellent match, BUT posting cannot be verified, info conflicts, old posting. Expected: fit=HIGH, opportunity_confidence=LOW, risk=MEDIUM, recommendation=APPLY_IF_TIME

Use a diverse set of realistic-sounding student profiles (CS students, data science, marketing, mechanical engineering, etc.) and realistic job descriptions (software engineer, data analyst, marketing intern, etc.).

Use synthetic company names that sound realistic (TechForge Solutions, DataPulse Inc, GreenLeaf Analytics, etc.) — do not use real company names.

Make job descriptions detailed and realistic — 3-8 bullet points for responsibilities, 4-8 required skills, 2-5 preferred skills.

Student profiles should vary — some have strong project experience, some have internship experience, some are fresh graduates.

The JSON must be valid, well-formatted, and the file should be written to disk.
